subject: pathology
title: Type 1 and Type 2 Diabetes, Insulitis, Insulin Resistance, HbA1c, and Microangiopathy

steps.tx: Type 1 diabetes autoimmunity destroys pancreatic beta cells through insulitis with islet antibodies, absolute insulin deficiency presenting ketoacidosis prone in youth yet any age. That autoimmune beta cell loss is **type 1 diabetes mellitus with insulitis**. HLA DR3 and DR4 haplotypes carry the strongest genetic risk, and enteroviral infection is the environmental trigger most often invoked in susceptible children.
steps.say: Autoimmune insulitis deletes beta cells; type 1 diabetes is absolute insulin failure at any age.

steps.tx: Insulitis infiltrates islets with lymphocytes in early type 1 diabetes rarely biopsied, antibodies GAD, IA2, ZnT8, and insulin predicting disease in relatives before glucose rises. Those predictive antibodies are **islet autoantibodies of type 1 diabetes**. Two or more positive antibodies define stage 1 disease even with normal glucose, and risk climbs steeply with each additional antibody specificity present.
steps.say: Islet antibodies predict type 1 diabetes years before glucose moves; staging now guides prevention trials.

steps.tx: Type 2 diabetes couples muscle liver adipose insulin resistance with progressive beta cell failure and islet amyloid from amylin co-secretion, hyperglycaemia emerging over silent years. That islet deposit is **islet amyloid polypeptide (amylin) in type 2 diabetes**. Congo red positive amyloid replaces islet tissue in most longstanding type 2 pancreases at autopsy, marking burnt out beta cell mass rather than active inflammation.
steps.say: Resistance plus failing beta cells plus amylin amyloid: type 2 diabetes in one islet sentence.

steps.tx: HbA1c glycates haemoglobin proportionally to average glucose over red cell lifespan, diagnosing and monitoring diabetes while anaemia, haemoglobin variants, and turnover falsify it. That averaged marker is **HbA1c (glycated haemoglobin)**. A value of 6.5 percent or more on two occasions makes the diagnosis, while recent transfusion or haemolysis should push the clinician toward fasting glucose instead.
steps.say: HbA1c averages three months of glucose unless red cells, variants, or pregnancy rewrite its maths.

steps.tx: Diabetic microangiopathy thickens capillary basement membranes in retina, kidney, and nerve through hyperglycaemic pathways, duration and control deciding who suffers its triopathy. That small vessel triad is **diabetic microangiopathy, retinopathy nephropathy neuropathy**. Nonenzymatic glycation, polyol pathway flux and protein kinase C activation converge on basement membrane thickening, which is why glucose control early matters more than late rescue.
steps.say: Retina, kidney, nerve: microangiopathy's triopathy follows glycaemic years and blood pressure together.

steps.tx: Hyaline arteriolosclerosis returns in diabetes affecting afferent and efferent glomerular arterioles, accelerating nephropathy beside hypertension's afferent pattern. That dual vessel change is **diabetic hyaline arteriolosclerosis, afferent and efferent**. Kimmelstiel Wilson nodules and a thickened glomerular basement membrane join it in classic diabetic nephropathy, with albuminuria usually preceding any fall in filtration rate.
steps.say: Diabetes hyalinises efferent arterioles too, a histological accent hypertension alone rarely gives.

steps.tx: Insulin resistance syndromes darken acanthosis nigricans, polycystic ovary associations, and metabolic syndrome cluster around waist, pressure, triglycerides, and glucose. That cluster is **metabolic syndrome of insulin resistance**. Velvety pigmented thickening in the neck and axillae, acanthosis nigricans, gives the skin level clue that severe insulin resistance is driving the metabolic picture.
steps.say: Waist, pressure, triglycerides, HDL, glucose: metabolic syndrome counts insulin resistance's companions.

steps.tx: Diabetic ketoacidosis and hyperosmolar states divide insulin absolute deficiency with ketones from severe dehydration hyperglycaemia without significant ketosis in type 2 disease. That emergency split is **DKA versus hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state**. Anion gap acidosis with ketones demands insulin infusion in DKA, whereas HHS mortality rides on dehydration and comorbidity, so cautious volume replacement leads there.
steps.say: Ketones plus acidosis mean DKA; extreme glucose, osmolality, dryness without ketones mean HHS.
